mainTopic: The end of the משנה's lament over the decline after the חורבן and in the time before the משיח, followed by the opening of the גמרא: which kinds of bridegroom crowns were banned (רב, שמואל, לוי).
overview: This amud finishes the משנה and the whole of מסכת סוטה. The משנה ends its lament over the decline after the חורבן. It then describes the dark time before the משיח: חוצפה, high prices, heresy in power, rotting Torah wisdom and families turning on each other. Twice it ends with the same answer: we can rely only on our Father in Heaven. The גמרא then goes back over the decrees from the time of the wars. רב, שמואל and לוי argue about which bridegroom crowns were banned. The גמרא also defines the forbidden drum, the brides' 'city of gold' crown and the gold-trimmed grooms' canopy. A ברייתא tells how a traitor's use of Greek wisdom during the חשמונאי civil war led to the curse on teaching it. The גמרא then separates the Greek language, which is allowed, from Greek wisdom, which is banned except for families close to the government, like רבן גמליאל's. Finally it explains the bride's covered carriage, lists the special greatness lost with each great חכם, and records רב יוסף and רב נחמן objecting to the last line before the הדרן closes the מסכת.

steps.title: The people keep declining and our only support is ה׳
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes its lament: the people keep declining, nobody seeks to fix it, and we can only rely on our Father in Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: The people keep going down and getting worse, and nobody asks about it or looks for a fix. Who can we lean on? Only on our Father in Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: We are in the middle of the משנה's sad list of what was lost after the בית המקדש was destroyed. This line closes that list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The decline has reached the ordinary people, not only the leaders. The worst part is that nobody even asks or searches for a fix. With no human source of help left, the משנה points to ה׳ alone.

keyTerms.meaning: To lean on, to rely on

phrases.english: keep going and declining,
phrases.notes: Still talking about the common people from the line before. The corrected wording leaves out the word in round brackets and uses the one in square brackets.

phrases.english: and no one asks and no one seeks.
Upon whom is there to rely?
Upon our Father in Heaven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's lament from the end of the previous section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The spiritual decline has spread to the people with no one seeking repair, so the only support left is ה׳.

steps.title: Signs of the time before the משיח: society and land
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists signs of the era just before the משיח: חוצפה, high prices, heresy in the government, and ruin and poverty in the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the משיח is getting close, חוצפה will grow and prices will shoot up. The vines will give fruit, but wine will still be expensive. The government will turn to heresy and nobody will rebuke it. The Sages' meeting place will become a place of immorality. The גליל will be destroyed, the Gavlan will be desolate, and the people of the border area will wander from town to town and find no pity.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה starts a new description: what the world will look like right before the משיח comes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each line shows something turned upside down. Even with plenty of fruit, wine is costly. The government should guard values but turns to heresy, and the place of Torah becomes a place of sin. Nobody is left to rebuke or to show mercy.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'the heels of the משיח': the time just before he comes

steps.confusionAlert: 'Footsteps of the משיח' is not about the משיח himself doing these things. It describes the troubled period right before he arrives.

phrases.english: In the footsteps of the Messiah
phrases.notes: This means the time when the משיח is about to come.

phrases.english: impudence will increase
and high prices will soar.
The vine will give its fruit
yet the wine will be expensive,
and the government will turn to heresy
and there will be no rebuke.
The meeting house will become a place of immorality
and the Galilee will be destroyed,
and the Gavlan will be desolate,
and the people of the border will wander from city to city
and no one will pity them,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the decline after the חורבן to a new description of the era before the משיח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The time before the משיח will be marked by חוצפה, high prices, heresy in power with no rebuke, and destruction and poverty in the land.

steps.title: Signs of the time before the משיח: Torah, truth and family
steps.stepSummary: The list goes on: Torah wisdom rots, the God-fearing are despised, truth disappears, and the young shame the old. Families fall apart, and again the only support is ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wisdom of the Torah scholars will rot. People who fear sin will be looked down on, and truth will be missing. Young people will embarrass the elders, and elders will have to stand up for the young. A son will disgrace his father, a daughter will rise against her mother, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law. A man's enemies will be his own household. The generation's face will be like a dog's face, and a son will feel no shame before his father. So what can we rely on? Only on our Father in Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues the same list of signs before the משיח. It moves to Torah, truth and respect between people, and it ends with the same line about relying on ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The breakdown now reaches values and the home. The proper order of respect is flipped, with elders standing for youngsters and children disgracing parents. Ending with 'our Father in Heaven' ties this back to step 1: when every human support breaks down, ה׳ remains.

keyTerms.meaning: The wisdom of the Torah scholars

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה ends twice with the same answer: when every human support collapses, we rely on אבינו שבשמים.

phrases.english: and the wisdom of the scribes will rot,
and those who fear sin will be despised,
and the truth will be missing.
Youths will shame the faces of elders,
elders will stand up before the young —
a son disgraces a father,
a daughter rises against her mother,
a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law,
phrases.notes: These family lines come from מיכה 7:6.

phrases.english: a man's enemies are the people of his own household,
the face of the generation is like the face of a dog,
the son is not ashamed before his father,
and upon what do we have to rely?
Upon our Father in Heaven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same list of signs before the משיח and closes it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before the משיח, Torah wisdom, truth and family respect will collapse, and our only support will be ה׳.

steps.title: רב: only crowns of salt and sulfur were banned
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's ban on bridegroom crowns. רב says it covers only crowns of salt and sulfur, while myrtle and rose crowns are allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: The ban was only on crowns made of salt and sulfur. Crowns of myrtle and roses are allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. It goes back to an earlier line in the משנה, the ban on bridegrooms' crowns, and רב limits how far that ban reaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the משנה said bridegroom crowns were banned, but it did not say which kinds. רב reads the ban narrowly. Only the salt-and-sulfur crowns are included, and flower crowns like myrtle and rose stay permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this about (limits a rule)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not commenting on the lament it just finished. It jumps back to the earlier line in the משנה about bridegroom crowns.

phrases.english: GEMARA. Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁל מֶלַח וְגׇפְרִית,
phrases.english: They taught this only about crowns of salt and sulfur,
phrases.notes: 'This' is the ban on bridegrooms' crowns from earlier in the משנה.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל שֶׁל הֲדַס וְשֶׁל וֶורֶד — מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: but those of myrtle and of rose are permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁל מֶלַח וְגׇפְרִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא by returning to an earlier ruling in the משנה, the ban on bridegroom crowns.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban on bridegroom crowns covers only crowns of salt and sulfur. Myrtle and rose crowns are permitted.

steps.title: שמואל: myrtle and rose are also banned, but reeds are allowed
steps.stepSummary: שמואל widens the ban to include myrtle and rose crowns, but he still permits crowns of reeds and bulrush.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל says: Even crowns of myrtle and roses are forbidden. Crowns of reeds and bulrush are allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a different view from רב about how wide the crown ban is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Where רב allowed flower crowns, שמואל forbids them too. He draws the line lower, at simple crowns of reeds and bulrush, which stay permitted.

phrases.english: And Shmuel says:

phrases.aramaic: אַף שֶׁל הֲדַס וְשֶׁל וֶורֶד אָסוּר,
phrases.english: Even those of myrtle and of rose are forbidden,
those of reeds and of bulrush are permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אוֹמֵר אַף שֶׁל הֲדַס וְשֶׁל וֶורֶד אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב and widens the ban.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Myrtle and rose crowns are also forbidden. Only reed and bulrush crowns are permitted.

steps.title: לוי: even crowns of reeds are banned
steps.stepSummary: לוי widens the ban the most: even crowns of reeds and bulrush are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי said: Even crowns of reeds and bulrush are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: A third view: לוי goes further than both רב and שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each view so far has added more to the ban. לוי includes even the simplest crowns of reeds and bulrush, which שמואל had permitted.

phrases.english: And Levi said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף שֶׁל קָנִים וְשֶׁל חִילָת אָסוּר.
phrases.english: Even those of reeds and of bulrush are forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵוִי אָמַר אַף שֶׁל קָנִים וְשֶׁל חִילָת אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes beyond שמואל and forbids even what שמואל permitted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even reed and bulrush crowns are forbidden.

steps.title: לוי's ברייתא matches his view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that לוי also taught this same ruling in his own collection of ברייתות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And that is how לוי taught it in his collection of teachings: Even crowns of reeds and bulrush are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up לוי's view by pointing out that his own ברייתא says the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לוי's view is not only his personal opinion. It also appears in the ברייתא collection he taught, which gives it the weight of a תנאי teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: And so he taught (introduces a supporting teaching)
His collection of ברייתות (teachings outside the משנה)

steps.whatToRemember: Three views on the crown ban, each wider than the one before. רב bans only salt and sulfur. שמואל adds myrtle and rose. לוי bans even reeds and bulrush, backed by his own ברייתא.

phrases.english: And so Levi taught in his collection of teachings:

phrases.aramaic: אַף שֶׁל קָנִים וְשֶׁל חִילָת אָסוּר.
phrases.english: Even those of reeds and of bulrush are forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports לוי's statement from step 6.
steps.raayaObject: לוי's view that even reed and bulrush crowns are forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: לוי's own ברייתא collection, which says the same ruling.

steps.title: What is the forbidden drum?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ban on the אירוס and asks what that word means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said they decreed against the אירוס. What is an אירוס?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא picks up the next item in the משנה's list of decrees and asks what the unusual word אירוס means. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on bridegroom crowns was already discussed in steps 4–7. Now the גמרא moves to the next word in the same line of the משנה. The word is unclear, so it needs a definition before any ruling can be understood.

keyTerms.meaning: A musical instrument the משנה says was banned, apparently a kind of drum
What is? (a question asking for a definition)

phrases.english: And on the irus.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה: the decree also covered the אירוס, along with bridegroom crowns.

phrases.english: What is an irus?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the bridegroom-crown discussion to the next item in the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word אירוס in the משנה

steps.title: A drum with one opening
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that the אירוס is a drum with only one open mouth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: It is a drum with one mouth.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the question: the banned instrument is a one-mouthed drum.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban is on a specific kind of drum, one whose skin covers only one side. Joyful music like this was stopped as a sign of mourning, so the exact type of instrument matters.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
A drum with one mouth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The אירוס is a one-mouthed drum

steps.title: רב הונא breaks his grandson's tambourine
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא made a tambourine for his son, and his father רב הונא broke it because it could be mistaken for the forbidden drum. He told him to make a drum over a jug or a measuring cup instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא made a tambourine for his son. His father came and broke it. He said to him: It can be confused with a one-mouthed drum. Go make him one on the mouth of a jug or on the mouth of a קפיזא measuring cup.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story showing how seriously the ban on the one-mouthed drum was taken. Even a child's tambourine was broken because it looked too much like the forbidden drum.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The tambourine itself was not the banned instrument. רב הונא worried that people would see it and think a one-mouthed drum is allowed. A skin stretched over a jug or a measuring cup looks clearly different, so there is no such mix-up.

keyTerms.meaning: It will be mistaken for something else

steps.confusionAlert: רב הונא did not break the tambourine because tambourines themselves are forbidden. He broke it only because people might confuse it with the banned one-mouthed drum.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna
made a tambourine for his son.
His father came and broke it.
phrases.notes: 'His father' is רב הונא, the father of רבה and grandfather of the child.

phrases.english: He said to him:
It will be confused with a drum with one mouth.
Go make it for him on the mouth of a jug
or on the mouth of a kefiza.
phrases.notes: A kefiza is a small measuring container. Stretching a skin over its opening makes a toy drum that looks different.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא עֲבַד לֵיהּ לִבְרֵיהּ טַנְבּוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the definition from step 9 being applied in real life
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anything that could be mistaken for a one-mouthed drum should be avoided. A drum made over a jug or a measuring cup is fine.

steps.title: What are brides' crowns?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's decree on brides' crowns during the war of טיטוס and asks what kind of crown is meant.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the war of טיטוס they decreed against brides' crowns. What are brides' crowns?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next decree in the משנה and asks what exactly counts as a 'bride's crown.' This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה bans brides' crowns but does not describe them. Without a definition we would not know whether every head covering a bride wears is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: The war of טיטוס, in which the second בית המקדש was destroyed

phrases.english: In the war of Titus
they decreed against brides' crowns, etc.
What are brides' crowns?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next decree in the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of crown the decree on brides' crowns covers

steps.title: A gold 'city' crown
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה, quoting רבי יוחנן, says a bride's crown means a 'city of gold.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: a city of gold.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers: the forbidden bride's crown is a 'city of gold.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: A 'city of gold' is a gold crown shaped or engraved like a city, probably ירושלים. So the ban targets a costly gold ornament, not every bridal head covering.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'city of gold': a gold crown designed like a city

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan:
A city of gold.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A bride's crown is a gold 'city' crown

steps.title: A ברייתא agrees, and allows a wool cap
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא also defines a bride's crown as a city of gold, and adds that the same shape may be made as a cap of fine wool.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught: Which are brides' crowns? A city of gold. But one may make it as a cap of fine wool.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רבי יוחנן's definition. It also tells us what a bride may still wear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא matches רבי יוחנן word for word: the banned crown is the gold 'city.' It adds something new: the same design made as a soft cap of fine wool is allowed. What was banned is the gold luxury, not the bridal headpiece itself.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (a ברייתא that supports the statement)

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
Which are brides' crowns?
A city of gold.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל עוֹשֶׂה אוֹתָהּ כִּיפָּה שֶׁל מֵילָת.
phrases.english: But one may make it as a cap of fine wool.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the definition given in step 12
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's definition of a bride's crown as a city of gold
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that gives the same definition
steps.whatToRemember: The bride's crown that was banned is a gold 'city' crown. The same thing made of fine wool is still allowed.

steps.title: They also banned grooms' canopies
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא adds that the חכמים also decreed against grooms' canopies.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: They also decreed against grooms' canopies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more decree that is not in the משנה, the ban on grooms' canopies. This sets up the question of what that means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This extends the משנה's list. It is surprising, since a wedding needs a חופה, so the next step has to explain what kind of canopy is meant.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנָא: אַף עַל חוּפַּת חֲתָנִים גָּזְרוּ.
phrases.english: It was taught: They decreed even against grooms' canopies.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: אַף עַל חוּפַּת חֲתָנִים גָּזְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another decree from the same period as the brides' crowns
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Grooms' canopies were also included in the decree

steps.title: Which canopy is meant?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'grooms' canopies' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are grooms' canopies?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which canopy is banned. It could not mean the wedding חופה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Weddings went on after the חורבן, so the decree cannot ban the חופה. The גמרא needs to identify the specific part that was forbidden.

phrases.english: What are grooms' canopies?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a definition of the decree in step 14
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly the forbidden 'grooms' canopy' is

steps.title: Gold-decorated crimson cloths
steps.stepSummary: The answer: grooms' canopies means crimson cloths decorated with gold.
steps.simpleTranslation: Gold-decorated crimson cloths.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ban is on the fancy gold-trimmed crimson cloths hung on the canopy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The decree targets the luxurious decoration, not the חופה itself. This fits the pattern of the brides' crowns, where only the gold version was banned.

phrases.english: Gold-decorated crimson cloths.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The banned canopy is made of gold-decorated crimson cloths

steps.title: A ברייתא agrees, and allows a papyrus frame
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא confirms the definition and adds that one may build a papyrus frame and hang anything he wants on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught: These are grooms' canopies: gold-decorated crimson cloths. But one may make a papyrus frame and hang on it whatever he wants.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports the definition and explains what is still allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא confirms that the ban is on the gold-trimmed crimson canopy. It adds that a simple papyrus structure is allowed, and he may hang whatever he likes on it. The concern was the specific grand canopy, not every decoration.

keyTerms.meaning: A frame or structure made of papyrus reeds

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
These are grooms' canopies:
gold-decorated crimson cloths.
But one may make a papyrus frame
and hang on it whatever he wants.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the definition in step 16, the same way step 13 supported step 12
steps.raayaObject: The definition of grooms' canopies as gold-decorated crimson cloths
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the same definition
steps.whatToRemember: Both decrees ban a specific luxury: the gold 'city' crown and the gold-trimmed crimson canopy. Simpler versions, a wool cap or a papyrus frame, are still allowed.

steps.title: The Hasmonean civil war begins the Greek story
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ban on teaching one's son Greek and begins a ברייתא about the siege between הורקנוס, outside, and אריסטובולוס, inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: and that one should not teach his son Greek. The חכמים taught: When the kings of the חשמונאי family besieged each other, הורקנוס was outside and אריסטובולוס was inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the משנה's ban on teaching Greek and starts telling the story behind it. This step sets the scene for what happens next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of defining a word, the גמרא explains where the decree came from. It begins with two חשמונאי brothers fighting over the throne, one besieging ירושלים from outside and one defending it from inside.

phrases.english: And that one should not teach his son Greek.
The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֶׁצָּרוּ מַלְכֵי בֵּית חַשְׁמוֹנַאי זֶה עַל זֶה,
phrases.english: When the kings of the Hasmonean house besieged each other,
Hyrcanus was outside,
phrases.notes: Outside the walls of ירושלים, besieging the city.

phrases.english: and Aristobulus was inside.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשֶׁלֹּא יְלַמֵּד אֶת בְּנוֹ יְווֹנִית. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new decree in the משנה and starts the story behind it
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The background of the Greek decree is the siege between הורקנוס and אריסטובולוס

steps.title: Coins down, offering animals up
steps.stepSummary: Every day, those inside lowered coins in a box, and those outside sent up animals for the daily offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: Each and every day they would lower dinars in a box, and they would send up animals for the daily offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues: even during the war, the two sides had a daily deal so the תמיד offering could still be brought. This sets up the turn in the story that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people inside the city needed animals for the תמיד but were cut off. So they paid the besiegers with coins lowered in a box, and the besiegers sent animals up. This daily arrangement is the background for what goes wrong next.

keyTerms.meaning: Animals for the daily offerings in the בית המקדש

phrases.english: Each and every day
they would lower dinars in a box,
and they would send up to them animals for the daily offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּכׇל יוֹם וָיוֹם הָיוּ מְשַׁלְשְׁלִין דִּינָרִים בְּקוּפָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the siege story from step 18
steps.mimraCoreRuling: During the siege, coins went down and animals for the תמיד came up every day

steps.title: The elder's secret hint and the pig on the wall
steps.stepSummary: An elder who knew Greek wisdom secretly told the besiegers that the city would not fall while the daily offerings went on. The next day they sent up a pig, and the land shook.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was an old man there who knew Greek wisdom. He hinted to the people outside in Greek wisdom: 'As long as they keep doing the Temple service, they will not be handed over to you.' The next day the people inside lowered coins in a box, and the people outside sent up a pig. When it got halfway up the wall, it dug its hooves in, and ארץ ישראל shook for four hundred parasangs.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues the siege story from the last step. A traitor uses Greek wisdom to pass a secret message, and the daily offerings are cut off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, both sides had kept the daily offering going through the coin-and-animal exchange. The elder's coded hint teaches the besiegers that the עבודה itself is protecting the city. So they stop it in the most insulting way possible, and the earthquake shows how serious this was.

keyTerms.meaning: Greek wisdom, a special kind of Greek learning that outsiders could not easily follow
Hinted or spoke in a foreign, coded way
The Temple service, here the daily offerings
Parasang, a large measure of distance

phrases.english: There was a certain elder there
who was familiar with Greek wisdom.
He hinted to them in Greek wisdom.
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the besiegers outside the wall. He used a code that only people trained in Greek wisdom would understand.

phrases.english: He said to them:
As long as they are busy with the Temple service,
they will not be handed over into your hands.
The next day they lowered coins to them in a box,
and they sent up a pig to them.
Once it reached halfway up the wall,
it dug in its hooves,
and the Land of Israel shook
for four hundred parasangs.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיָה שָׁם זָקֵן אֶחָד שֶׁהָיָה מַכִּיר בְּחׇכְמַת יְווֹנִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the siege story: the arrangement for the daily offerings is broken.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Greek wisdom was used to betray the city, and the daily offering was replaced by a pig.

steps.title: The curse on raising pigs and teaching Greek wisdom
steps.stepSummary: Because of what happened, the חכמים cursed anyone who raises pigs or teaches his son Greek wisdom.
steps.simpleTranslation: At that time they said: Cursed is a person who raises pigs, and cursed is a person who teaches his son Greek wisdom.
steps.whatsHappening: The story reaches its point. The חכמים make two curses that match the two things that caused the disaster.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each curse matches part of the story: the pig replaced the offering, and Greek wisdom carried the traitor's message. This is the source for the משנה's ban on teaching one's son Greek, which was quoted in step 18.
steps.whatToRemember: The ban is tied to Greek wisdom, because that was what the traitor used. Keep this in mind for the question that comes next.

phrases.english: At that time they said:
Cursed is a person who raises pigs,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָרוּר אָדָם שֶׁיְּלַמֵּד לִבְנוֹ חׇכְמַת יְווֹנִית.
phrases.english: and cursed is a person who teaches his son Greek wisdom.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the legal lesson from the story just told.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Raising pigs and teaching one's son Greek wisdom are both placed under a curse.

steps.title: That year the offerings came from unusual places
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds a teaching about that same year: the עומר and the שתי הלחם had to come from unusual places.
steps.simpleTranslation: About that year we learned: It once happened that the עומר came from גגות צריפים, and the two loaves came from the valley of עין סוכר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא connects a teaching found elsewhere to this same year, to show how badly the land suffered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally there would be no need to record where these offerings came from. Recording that they came from these particular places shows that the usual fields could not supply them that year.

keyTerms.meaning: The barley offering brought on the sixteenth of ניסן
The two wheat loaves offered on שבועות

phrases.english: And about that year we learned:
It once happened that the omer came from Gaggot Tzerifim,
and the two loaves came from the valley of Ein Sokher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another detail about the same year as the siege.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: That year the עומר and שתי הלחם were brought from unusual places.

steps.title: But רבי and רב יוסף praised Greek and Persian
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ban on Greek. רבי said people in ארץ ישראל should speak Hebrew or Greek, and רב יוסף said people in בבל should speak Hebrew or Persian.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? Didn't רבי say: Why speak Syriac in ארץ ישראל? Speak either the holy language or Greek! And רב יוסף said: Why speak Aramaic in בבל? Speak either the holy language or Persian!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ban. If Greek is so bad, why did רבי recommend speaking it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה and the ברייתא sound like Greek is completely forbidden. But רבי actually preferred Greek over the everyday Aramaic. רב יוסף's similar statement about Persian is brought to show the same kind of attitude.

keyTerms.meaning: Syriac, the Aramaic spoken in ארץ ישראל
Persian, the language of the rulers in בבל

phrases.english: Is that so?
But didn't Rabbi say:
phrases.notes: 'רבי' with no name means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: In the Land of Israel, why use the Syriac language?
Rather, either the holy language
or the Greek language.
And Rav Yosef said:
In Babylonia, why use the Aramaic language?
Rather, either the holy language
or the Persian language!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ban on Greek that was just established.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי recommended speaking Greek, so how can Greek be forbidden?

steps.title: The Greek language is different from Greek wisdom
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the Greek language and Greek wisdom are two separate things. Only Greek wisdom was banned.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Greek language is one thing, and Greek wisdom is another thing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by separating two things that seemed to be the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי praised the Greek language itself, meaning speaking Greek. The curse was only on Greek wisdom, the special learning the traitor used to send his secret message. So there is no contradiction.
steps.whatToRemember: Speaking the Greek language is allowed and even praised. Only Greek wisdom was banned.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read the curse as a ban on knowing the Greek language. The text clearly says Greek wisdom.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical limit of the ban: the language itself is not forbidden.

phrases.english: The Greek language is one thing,
and Greek wisdom is another thing.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְשׁוֹן יְווֹנִית לְחוּד, וְחׇכְמַת יְווֹנִית לְחוּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רבי and רב יוסף.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ban covers anything Greek, including the language.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only Greek wisdom is banned. The Greek language is allowed.

steps.title: Was Greek wisdom really forbidden? Half of רבן גמליאל's household studied it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ban on Greek wisdom. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said that five hundred children in his father's house learned Greek wisdom.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is Greek wisdom really forbidden? רבן שמעון בן גמליאל explained the פסוק 'My eye affected my soul, because of all the daughters of my city.' He said there were a thousand children in his father's house. Five hundred learned תורה and five hundred learned Greek wisdom. Only he survived in ארץ ישראל, and one cousin survived in Asia.
steps.whatsHappening: Step 24 said only Greek wisdom was banned, not the Greek language. Now the גמרא asks how Greek wisdom could be banned if the household of the נשיא openly taught it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is no longer an attack on the Greek language. It targets Greek wisdom itself. A great leader like רבן גמליאל would not have had half his household study something forbidden, so the ban seems to be contradicted.

keyTerms.meaning: Greek wisdom: Greek learning and clever ways of speaking, as opposed to just the Greek language
Is it really forbidden? This is a challenging question.
But didn't he say...? This opens a source that contradicts what was just said.
My eye affected my soul. A פסוק from איכה about grief.

phrases.english: And is Greek wisdom really forbidden?
But didn't Rav Yehuda say that Shmuel said
in the name of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"My eye affected my soul
because of all the daughters of my city"
There were a thousand children in my father's house
Five hundred learned Torah
and five hundred learned Greek wisdom

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא נִשְׁתַּיֵּיר מֵהֶן אֶלָּא אֲנִי כָּאן
phrases.english: and none of them survived except me, here
and my father's brother's son, in Asia!
phrases.notes: עסיא is a place outside ארץ ישראל. The cousin survived far away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 24, which narrowed the ban to Greek wisdom only.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ban on teaching Greek wisdom (steps 21 and 24)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The household of the נשיא had five hundred children studying Greek wisdom. A great leader would not allow something forbidden, so Greek wisdom seems to be permitted.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל's family was different because they dealt with the government
steps.stepSummary: The family of רבן גמליאל was a special exception because they were close to the ruling power.
steps.simpleTranslation: The house of רבן גמליאל is different, because they were close to the government.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The ban on Greek wisdom stays in place, but רבן גמליאל's family had a special exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The family had to speak with Roman officials, so they needed Greek wisdom to do their work for the community. This is an exception for one family, not a cancellation of the ban.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different. This marks a special case.
Close to the government, people who deal with the rulers

steps.confusionAlert: Do not conclude that Greek wisdom is permitted. The ban still stands. Only people who must deal with the government received an exception.

phrases.english: The house of Rabban Gamliel is different
because they were close to the government.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 25.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because the נשיא's household studied Greek wisdom, it seemed to be permitted for everyone.
steps.terutzMaskana: Greek wisdom is forbidden in general. Families who deal with the government were given an exception.

steps.title: Proof from a ברייתא: people close to the government got special permission
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that people close to the government were allowed things others were not: a gentile haircut for אבטולוס בן ראובן, and Greek wisdom for רבן גמליאל's family.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches that cutting your hair in the 'קומי' style is one of the ways of the אמורי, which we may not copy. Still, אבטולוס בן ראובן was allowed to cut his hair that way because he was close to the government. The house of רבן גמליאל was also allowed Greek wisdom, because they were close to the government.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove the answer of step 26. The ברייתא states exactly this exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives a parallel case: a gentile hairstyle is normally forbidden, but it was allowed for someone who had to appear before the rulers. It then names רבן גמליאל's house and Greek wisdom directly, which confirms the answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Cutting hair in the 'komi' style, a gentile fashion
The ways of the אמורי, gentile customs that a Jew should not copy

steps.whatToRemember: Greek wisdom stays forbidden. People who must deal with the government, like רבן גמליאל's family, were given an exception.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita:
One who cuts his hair in the komi style
this is one of the ways of the Emorites.
Avtolos ben Reuven:
they permitted him to cut his hair komi style,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets, "to him," is part of the corrected wording.

phrases.english: because he is close to the government.
The house of Rabban Gamliel:
they permitted them Greek wisdom,
because they are close to the government.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 26 with an explicit ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The answer that רבן גמליאל's house had a special exception
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that permits the komi haircut to אבטולוס בן ראובן and Greek wisdom to רבן גמליאל's house, both because they were close to the government

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: the decree against a bride's covered carriage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: in the last war the חכמים decreed that a bride may not go out in a covered carriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the last war they decreed that a bride may not go out in a covered carriage, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה. This step only quotes it, to set up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'and so on' points to the rest of the משנה, which says our רבנן later allowed a bride to ride in a carriage inside the city. The גמרא is about to explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: A covered carriage or litter for carrying a bride
And so on. The rest of the quoted text continues.

phrases.english: In the last war they decreed
that a bride may not go out in a covered carriage, etc.
phrases.notes: The "etc." stands for the rest of the משנה: our רבנן later allowed it inside the city.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the last war a bride was forbidden to ride in a covered carriage. Later it was allowed inside the city.

steps.title: Asking for the reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the ruling about the bride's carriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question about the משנה it just quoted. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack. The גמרא simply wants to know why the later חכמים allowed the carriage again.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: He is asking why the later רבנן allowed the bride to ride in the carriage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the משנה quoted in step 28.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the later רבנן permitted a bride to ride in a covered carriage

steps.title: Because of modesty
steps.stepSummary: It was allowed for the sake of modesty.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of modesty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The carriage was allowed for the sake of modesty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Riding in a covered carriage keeps the bride from being seen by everyone in the street. That modesty is why the later חכמים allowed it inside the city.

phrases.english: Because of modesty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The carriage was permitted so the bride would be covered and modest, not on display in the street.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: when רבן יוחנן died, wisdom ceased
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: when רבן יוחנן בן זכאי died, wisdom ceased.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבן יוחנן died, wisdom ceased.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to another line of the משנה about what was lost when great חכמים died. It quotes the line to set up the ברייתא that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists great חכמים and the special quality that was lost with each one. This line is about רבן יוחנן בן זכאי and his wisdom.

keyTerms.meaning: From the time that he died
It ceased, came to an end

phrases.english: When Rabban Yoḥanan died, wisdom ceased.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The death of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי marked the end of his kind of wisdom.

steps.title: A ברייתא: what was lost when רבי אליעזר, רבי יהושע and רבי עקיבא died
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא adds to the משנה's list: each of these great חכמים took a special kind of תורה greatness with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: When רבי אליעזר died, the ספר תורה was hidden away. When רבי יהושע died, good advice and deep thinking ended. When רבי עקיבא died, the strong arms of תורה ended and the springs of wisdom were sealed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that continues the משנה's list. It describes what was lost with three more great חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each description matches the חכם's special strength. רבי אליעזר's death is pictured as burying a ספר תורה. With רבי יהושע, deep counsel ended. With רבי עקיבא, the powerful explaining of the תורה ended.

keyTerms.meaning: The arms of תורה, its strength

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה and ברייתא describe each great חכם by the special gift that was lost when he died: wisdom, a living ספר תורה, deep counsel, and the strength and springs of תורה.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: מִשֶּׁמֵּת רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר נִגְנַז סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה.
phrases.english: When Rabbi Eliezer died, the Torah scroll was hidden away.
When Rabbi Yehoshua died,
advice and deep thinking ceased.
When Rabbi Akiva died,
the arms of Torah ceased
and the springs of wisdom were sealed.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִשֶּׁמֵּת רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר נִגְנַז סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the משנה's list from step 31 with a ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The deaths of רבי אליעזר, רבי יהושע and רבי עקיבא each ended a special kind of תורה greatness.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה and the crowns of wisdom
steps.stepSummary: When רבי אלעזר בן עזריה died, the crowns of wisdom ended, based on a פסוק linking the crown of the wise with riches.
steps.simpleTranslation: From when רבי אלעזר בן עזריה died, the crowns of wisdom ended, as the פסוק says: 'The crown of the wise is their riches.'
steps.whatsHappening: The list from the previous step continues. The next name is רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, and with him the 'crowns of wisdom' ended.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each entry in this list pairs one חכם with one kind of greatness that ended when he died. Here the greatness is called 'crowns of wisdom', and a פסוק is brought to connect a wise person's crown with riches.

phrases.english: From when Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya died
the crowns of wisdom ceased,
as "the crown of the wise is their riches."

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשֶּׁמֵּת רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה בָּטְלוּ עַטְרוֹת חׇכְמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of חכמים begun in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's death, the crowns of wisdom ended.

steps.title: רבי חנינא בן דוסא and אבא יוסי בן קטונתא
steps.stepSummary: When רבי חנינא בן דוסא died, men of deeds ended. When אבא יוסי בן קטונתא died, the pious ended.
steps.simpleTranslation: From when רבי חנינא בן דוסא died, men of deeds ended. From when אבא יוסי בן קטונתא died, the pious people ended.
steps.whatsHappening: The list continues with two more names. Each one is matched with the special quality that ended with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא בן דוסא stands for 'men of deeds' (אנשי מעשה), and אבא יוסי בן קטונתא stands for the חסידים. His unusual name is about to be explained in the next step.

phrases.english: From when Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa died
the men of deeds ceased.
From when Abba Yosei ben Katonta died
the pious ceased,

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשֶּׁמֵּת רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן דּוֹסָא בָּטְלוּ אַנְשֵׁי מַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the next two names to the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Men of deeds ended with רבי חנינא בן דוסא, and the pious ended with אבא יוסי בן קטונתא.

steps.title: Why was he called בן קטונתא?
steps.stepSummary: The text asks why אבא יוסי was called 'בן קטונתא'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why was he called אבא יוסי בן קטונתא?
steps.whatsHappening: The text stops to ask about the meaning of this חכם's name. It is setting up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name 'קטונתא' sounds like the word for 'small'. The question asks what this name has to do with him, since he is listed as the last of the חסידים.

keyTerms.meaning: and why was his name called

phrases.english: And why was he called
Abba Yosei ben Katonta?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָמָּה נִקְרָא שְׁמוֹ אַבָּא יוֹסֵי בֶּן קְטוֹנְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the name just mentioned.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning behind the name 'בן קטונתא'.

steps.title: He lived when the pious had become few
steps.stepSummary: He was called this because he was one of the 'diminished' pious people.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he was one of the 'small', or diminished, pious people.
steps.whatsHappening: The text answers the question: his name hints that he was among the pious people at a time when they had become few.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name קטונתא is read as connected to קטני, meaning 'small' or 'diminished'. So the name itself fits the idea that with him the חסידים came to an end.

phrases.english: Because he was among the diminished of the pious.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the name.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The name hints that he was among the last, diminished group of pious people.

steps.title: בן עזאי and בן זומא
steps.stepSummary: When בן עזאי died, the diligent learners ended. When בן זומא died, the expounders ended.
steps.simpleTranslation: From when בן עזאי died, the diligent ended. From when בן זומא died, the expounders ended.
steps.whatsHappening: The list returns after the name explanation and adds two more חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בן עזאי stands for constant, diligent learning, and בן זומא stands for skill in דרשה, explaining פסוקים. These are two different kinds of תורה greatness.

phrases.english: From when ben Azzai died
the diligent ceased;
from when ben Zoma died
the expounders ceased.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the list after explaining the name.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Diligence ended with בן עזאי, and skill in expounding ended with בן זומא.

steps.title: Troubles after רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and רבי
steps.stepSummary: When רבן שמעון בן גמליאל died, locusts came and troubles grew. When רבי died, troubles doubled.
steps.simpleTranslation: From when רבן שמעון בן גמליאל died, locusts came up and troubles increased. From when רבי died, troubles doubled.
steps.whatsHappening: The list changes direction: instead of a good quality ending, it now describes troubles that came to the world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now each entry said a type of greatness 'ceased'. Here the deaths bring something bad instead: locusts and troubles, and after רבי the troubles became double.

phrases.english: From when Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel died
locusts came up and troubles increased.
From when Rabbi died, troubles were doubled.
phrases.notes: 'רבי' with no name means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשֶּׁמֵּת רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל עָלָה גּוֹבַאי וְרַבּוּ צָרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list, now describing troubles instead of lost qualities.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Troubles increased after רבן שמעון בן גמליאל died and doubled after רבי died.

steps.title: With רבי, humility and fear of sin ended
steps.stepSummary: The last line of the משנה: when רבי died, humility and fear of sin ended.
steps.simpleTranslation: From when רבי died, humility and fear of sin ended.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the last line of the משנה's list. It is setting up the reactions of רב יוסף and רב נחמן that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line names two qualities that ended with רבי: ענוה and יראת חטא. The next two steps will each push back on one of these words.

phrases.english: From when Rabbi died
humility and fear of sin ceased.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשֶּׁמֵּת רַבִּי בָּטְלָה עֲנָוָה וְיִרְאַת חֵטְא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the final line of the משנה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When רבי died, humility and fear of sin ended.

steps.title: רב יוסף: do not teach that humility ended
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף tells the תנא not to recite 'humility', because he himself is still here.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said to the תנא: Do not teach 'humility', because I am still here.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף objects to the wording of the משנה. He says humility did not end, since he is still alive and has it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This targets one word of the line, 'ענוה'. רב יוסף asks that it be taken out of the recited text, because a humble person still exists.

keyTerms.meaning: the reciter of משניות and ברייתות in the בית מדרש

steps.confusionAlert: It sounds strange to claim to be humble about yourself. The גמרא gives no explanation here; just see that the point is a request to change the wording of the משנה.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said to the tanna:
phrases.notes: The תנא is the one who recited the משניות out loud in the בית מדרש.

phrases.english: Do not teach 'humility',
for there is me.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יוֹסֵף לְתַנָּא לָא תִּיתְנֵי עֲנָוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the word 'ענוה' in the line just quoted.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the word 'ענוה' in the משנה's last line.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Humility did not end, because רב יוסף still has it.

steps.title: רב נחמן: do not teach that fear of sin ended
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן tells the תנא not to recite 'fear of sin', because he himself is still here.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to the תנא: Do not teach 'fear of sin', because I am still here.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן makes the same kind of objection about the second word in the line, 'fear of sin'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Together with רב יוסף, both qualities in the last line are challenged. רב יוסף took on humility, and רב נחמן takes on fear of sin.
steps.whatToRemember: The list closes the מסכת by naming the greatness lost with each חכם. רב יוסף and רב נחמן each say one quality from the last line still exists in himself.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to the tanna:
Do not teach 'fear of sin',
for there is me.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן לְתַנָּא לָא תִּיתְנֵי יִרְאַת חֵטְא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same objection as רב יוסף, now about the second quality.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the words 'יראת חטא' in the משנה's last line.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Fear of sin did not end, because רב נחמן still has it.

steps.title: Hadran: closing פרק עגלה ערופה and מסכת סוטה
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for פרק עגלה ערופה and for all of מסכת סוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק עגלה ערופה, and מסכת סוטה is finished.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the formal closing line. It ends the פרק and the whole מסכת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No new teaching is added here. The הדרן expresses the wish to come back to this learning, and it marks the end of מסכת סוטה.

keyTerms.meaning: name of this פרק, the calf whose neck is broken

phrases.english: We will return to you, Egla Arufa,
and Tractate Sotah is concluded.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַרַן עֲלָךְ עֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה וּסְלִיקָא לַהּ מַסֶּכֶת סוֹטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק and the מסכת after the final discussion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: פרק עגלה ערופה and מסכת סוטה are complete.
